program_overview.title: Queen Coders
program_overview.tagline: The step from good developer to trusted engineer: architecture, AI engineering and technical leadership, built deliberately in nine months.
program_overview.description:
There is a career moment where writing good code stops being enough: teams need architecture judgment, security thinking, AI fluency and the leadership skills that turn seniority into influence. Queen Coders builds that step deliberately, for women developers, in a room of peers on the same climb.

The arc runs in three movements. Advanced engineering: software design principles at depth, cloud architecture, data architecture, performance and security, the judgment layer above syntax. AI engineering: machine learning engineering, modern AI applications, LLMs and agent development, the layer every senior role now assumes. Technical leadership: the honest skills of staff-level work, technical decision records, code review leadership, mentoring, engineering management versus the senior IC road, taught practically rather than aspirationally.

Nine months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more months in hand. Homework, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam, an architecture defense, that decides the certificate with a free retest. Real engineering, real leadership, no crowns required.
what_makes_this_different: The judgment layer: architecture, security and performance as decisions, not buzzwords
AI engineering included seriously: ML engineering, LLMs and agents, the layer senior roles now assume
Technical leadership taught practically: ADRs, review leadership, mentoring, the staff-vs-management fork
A peer room of women on the same climb, which changes what gets asked and answered
An honest 9-month arc with 2 months in hand
Real assessment: monthly mixed reviews and a final architecture defense that decides the certificate, with a free retest

faqs.question: What is Queen Coders, and who is it for?
faqs.answer: An advanced course for women developers with working experience (roughly 2+ years or a strong portfolio) building the step from good developer to trusted engineer: architecture and security judgment, AI engineering with LLMs and agents, and practical technical leadership, ending in an architecture dossier defended before a panel.

faqs.question: I am a developer but not "senior". Is this too early?
faqs.answer: If you can build and ship features independently, this is exactly the right time: the course teaches the judgment layer that turns feature-builders into engineers trusted with systems. A short conversation before enrolment places you honestly; Princess Coders graduates typically join after a period of real building.

faqs.question: How is leadership taught without becoming motivational fluff?
faqs.answer: Through artifacts and practice: architecture decision records written and defended, code reviews led live, mentoring practiced on real juniors from our other courses, and the management-versus-senior-IC fork examined with honest trade-offs. Every leadership week produces something reviewable.

faqs.question: How is progress assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Homework follows every class, each month ends with an assignment that deliberately mixes new questions with earlier topics, every phase closes with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: What comes after Queen Coders?
faqs.answer: Senior and staff-level work, entered with a defended dossier in hand; Alpha Girls for women who want the deepest technical road, systems at scale; or engineering management, chosen consciously. The peer room tends to persist, which is quietly the most valuable outcome.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, with 2 live classes a week in batches capped at 10 learners. A mini batch of 3-4 learners is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International learners pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.
